To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oncologists are supportive of the inclusion of health-related quality of live outcomes in clinical trials but that they perceive important barriers to its use in clinical decision-making, and that combined reporting of quality of life and clinical data may facilitate their use in practice.

(1) oncologists support the use of quality of life findings (QoL) from randomized controlled trials (RTCs) to inform practice; however, (2) they rarely use QoL findings in practice; and (3) they perceive important barriers to using QoL findings, such as a lack of time and understanding, and concerns over generalizability of QoL results.
